sentence_stem: I have already finished my homework,
correct_completion: so I can watch a film tonight.
full_sentence: I have already finished my homework, so I can watch a film tonight.
acceptable_variants: so I can relax this evening.
so I have free time tonight.

options.text: so I am still writing my essay.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'already finished', which says the homework is done.

options.text: I have just started a new project.
options.why_wrong: 'Just' refers to a very recent action. It does not give a logical result of the finished homework.

options.text: so I am going to sleep early.
options.why_wrong: This is possible, but it does not follow logically from the homework being finished in the way the stem sets up.

options.text: so I can watch a film tonight.

grammar_focus: Present perfect with 'already' in a result clause
explanation: With 'already', the present perfect shows that an action is complete before the present moment, and the second clause gives a logical result. Polish speakers often use a simple past form in this position, which does not work with 'already', so the present perfect needs focused practice.
translation: Prace domowe są już skończone, więc dziś wieczorem mogę obejrzeć film.
